text.p: Brazilian telephone holding Telebras SA rebounded from a recent decline Monday to stand out among American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Telebras was up 1-13/16 at 154-1/2 in moderate volume. The ADRs were among the most-active issues on the New York Stock Exchange.
Traders said Telebras was seeing a technical rebound. The high-flying stock has fallen from a recent 12-month high of 169-1/4 after rising from a low of 69.
"This is really a technical bounce, since something like seven houses have recently downgraded the ADR," a trader said.
"Also, there's a concern here that local mutual funds, which piled onto the market (for Telebras and other Brazilian shares), are going to pile right out again."

MCI Communications Corp also announced Monday that it, Telebras and British Telecommunications Plc would launch Concert Communications Services in Brazil by September. British Telecom was up 1-5/16 to 77-5/8.
Underlining the recent surge by Telebras, Lipper Analytical Services said in a July 11 report that Latin American mutual funds last week rose 3.7 percent for a year-to-date return of 44.31 percent.
Brazil and Mexico were the driving forces behind the rise, the report said.
Leading British pharmaceutical ADRs rose to 12-month highs, boosted by speculation that they could become takeover targets.
Glaxo Wellcome rose 1-12/16 to 46-7/16 and Zeneca rose 3-7/16 to 109. SmithKline Beecham Plc was up two to 104-5/8.
Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc rose 4-5/8 to 60-7/8 after the chemicals giant agreed to sell most of its bulk chemicals business to DuPont Co.
Decliners led advancers 200 to 193 among 814 ADRs in mid-morning. The ADR group was up 0.16 percent and volume was 13 million ADRs.
ADRs allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
